title: Bug: [Err Log] [SmartSwitch] [HA] ERR swss#orchagent: :- addHaScopeEntry: HA Set entry does not exist for haset0_0
author: vivekkarri
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Medium

### Description of the bug

During `test_ha_dpu_failure[Standby DPU Fail-Standby Traffic]`, after standby DPU reboot/restart, `orchagent` receives `DASH_HA_SCOPE_TABLE|haset0_0` entries without a preceding `DASH_HA_SET_TABLE|haset0_0` entry. Since the HA set is not present in `DashHaOrch::m_ha_set_entries`, `addHaScopeEntry()` logs repeated errors.

### Steps to Reproduce

Run:

python3 -m pytest ha/test_ha_dpu_power_down.py 

Relevant test case:

test_ha_dpu_failure[Standby DPU Fail-Standby Traffic]

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

Actual: after standby DPU restart, `swss.rec` shows `DASH_HA_SCOPE_TABLE|haset0_0` issued from HaMgrD without `DASH_HA_SET_TABLE|haset0_0`, causing repeated `orchagent` errors.

Expected: HA set config should be given before HA scope config

### Relevant log output

```
2026 Jun 23 15:17:56 smartswitch-dpu-0 ERR swss#orchagent: :- addHaScopeEntry: HA Set entry does not exist for haset0_0
2026 Jun 23 15:18:46 smartswitch-dpu-0 WARNING swss#orchagent: :- convertKfvToHaScopePb: Unknown field ha_term in HA Scope entry
2026 Jun 23 15:18:46 smartswitch-dpu-0 ERR swss#orchagent: :- addHaScopeEntry: HA Set entry does not exist for haset0_0
```

swss.rec evidence:

```
2026-06-23.15:17:47.077819|recording started
2026-06-23.15:17:56.404692|DASH_HA_SCOPE_TABLE|haset0_0|SET|version:1|ha_set_id:haset0_0|ha_role:standalone|ha_term:3
2026-06-23.15:17:56.404723|DASH_HA_SCOPE_TABLE|haset0_0|SET|ha_role:dead|version:1|ha_term:3|ha_set_id:haset0_0
```

No post-reboot `DASH_HA_SET_TABLE|haset0_0|SET` appears before these scope entries.

### Output of `show version`, `show techsupport`

Version: master, 202605

### Attach files (if any)

_No response_

comments.author: BYGX-wcr
comments.body: After the DPU is power down, it lost all HA entries in DPU_APPL_DB. However, hamgrd is unaware of this (because of the limitations of current monitoring system). When hamgrd tried to shut down the HA scope at the end of the test, it only programs a HA scope entry instead of reprogramming the HA set entry.

linkedPullRequests.title: swss-common-bridge: replay unchanged producer updates
linkedPullRequests.author: BYGX-wcr
linkedPullRequests.body:
### Description of PR

Summary:
The producer bridge cached the last update and skipped identical requests. That cache can outlive a DPU control-plane reset, so an HA_SET entry removed from the destination DB was not restored when hamgrd replayed unchanged data. Always apply valid producer requests so replay can recover externally lost DB state. Consumer-side caching remains unchanged.

Fixes: https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/28073

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / cleanup
- [ ] Documentation update
- [x] Test improvement

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?

A DPU control-plane reset can clear DASH_HA_SET_TABLE while swss-common-bridge remains running. Replaying the same HA_SET data previously returned "No change in data" without writing it, leaving the destination DB entry missing.

#### How did you do it?

- Removed producer-side TableCache deduplication.
- Apply every valid Set or Del request to the ProducerTable.
- Kept TableCache for consumer-side incremental merge and duplicate-notification filtering.
- Updated duplicate and ZMQ consumer-recreation tests to require identical updates to be replayed.

#### How did you verify/test it?

- `cargo fmt --check --all`
- `cargo build --workspace --all-features`
- `cargo test -p swss-common-bridge` (9 passed)
- Built the Debian runtime and debug-symbol packages.
- Installed and verified the packages in dash-hadpu0 through dash-hadpu3 on two SmartSwitches.
- Completed config reload on both switches and verified all eight hamgrd processes were running.

#### Any platform specific information?

Validated on SONiC SmartSwitch DPU containers using both Redis ProducerStateTable and ZmqProducerStateTable paths.

### Documentation

No documentation change is required; this restores producer replay correctness without changing the public interface.
